resources.name: Misk Launchpad
resources.discovery_method: Review testimonials, cohort announcements, alumni stories, and current participant spotlights; then verify founders by exact name.
resources.expected_yield: High volume of idea, prototype, MVP, and early-launch teams; named testimonials provide direct founder seeds.
resources.notes: Program eligibility explicitly includes idea, prototype, MVP, and early-launch startups committed to Saudi Arabia. Current page names Swarm Robotics, Dentophilic, Nitx, and Athleads founders.

evidence.paraphrase: The program targets Saudi-committed technology teams from idea through early launch and publishes named founder testimonials and program outcomes.

resources.name: The Garage accelerator and incubator
resources.discovery_method: Monitor accelerator, incubator, MVP Lab, hosted-program, and event announcements; harvest named participating ventures and founders from graduation posts.
resources.expected_yield: Large recurring pool of prototype, MVP, growth, and international ventures entering Saudi Arabia.
resources.notes: The public home page reports 950+ graduated startups and distinguishes MVP-stage incubation from growth-stage acceleration, but it does not expose a crawlable startup directory.

evidence.paraphrase: The Garage describes an incubator for prototype or MVP teams, an accelerator for completed products, and hosted programs; it reports more than 950 program graduates.

resources.name: Flat6Labs Riyadh Seed Program
resources.discovery_method: Monitor KSA program and press pages for cycle openings, investment announcements, demo days, and company profiles.
resources.cadence: monthly and at each cycle/demo day
resources.expected_yield: Roughly ten named early-stage technology startups per cycle, often with founder, product, pricing, and customer detail.
resources.notes: Cycle 5 and Cycle 6 produced the strongest candidate evidence in this lane.

evidence.paraphrase: The KSA page identifies the active Riyadh Seed Program and states that it supports more than 20 Saudi startups annually with seed funding.

resources.name: Flat6Labs Riyadh Demo Day pages
resources.discovery_method: At each demo day, extract every company, named CEO/founder, product, business model, target customer, and company profile link.
resources.expected_yield: Nine to ten named Saudi ventures per page with unusually rich qualification fields.
resources.notes: Cycle 5 took place on 2025-09-17, just after the preferred cutoff. The official page exposes nine complete founder/product profiles.

evidence.source_title: Flat6Labs Fifth Demo Day in Riyadh
evidence.paraphrase: The demo-day directory names each startup and CEO and provides product, business-model, industry, and target-customer descriptions.

evidence.source_title: Meet the Startups Pitching at our 5th Demo Day in Riyadh
evidence.paraphrase: Flat6Labs identifies the nine KSA-based Cycle 5 companies and says they spent four months developing their products before the September 17, 2025 showcase.

resources.name: KAUST TAQADAM Startup Accelerator
resources.geography: Saudi Arabia with international participants entering the Kingdom
resources.discovery_method: Monitor the accelerator home page and KAUST news for accepted cohorts, showcase finalists, grants, and Saudi-market commitments.
resources.expected_yield: Twenty ventures per recent cohort, with ten receiving follow-on awards and strong official product summaries.
resources.notes: The ninth cohort concluded in May 2026; every participant received $40,000 and ten received an additional $100,000.

evidence.paraphrase: TAQADAM describes a six-month accelerator with mentorship, network access, a $40,000 grant for teams, and potential $100,000 follow-on funding.

resources.name: KAUST TAQADAM showcase announcements
resources.discovery_method: Extract finalist companies from annual KAUST showcase releases, then verify founder, product maturity, team capacity, and actual Saudi operations on first-party company pages.
resources.cadence: annual showcase plus quarterly news checks
resources.expected_yield: Ten high-signal funded finalists per annual showcase.
resources.notes: Cohort inclusion proves accelerator participation and Saudi ecosystem intent, not Saudi incorporation or low technical capacity; those require separate verification.

evidence.source_title: KAUST and SAB celebrate milestone ninth cohort of TAQADAM accelerator
evidence.paraphrase: KAUST names ten follow-on-funded finalists from a 20-company cohort preparing to scale within Saudi Arabia's economy.

resources.name: CODE Software Accelerator
resources.discovery_method: Monitor CODE quarterly reports and challenge pages for software-accelerator graduates, demo days, and named health-tech or sector challenge finalists.
resources.expected_yield: Ten-plus early-stage integrated-software companies when a cohort directory is published.
resources.notes: The official report proves the program format and cohort size but does not list the participating companies in crawlable text.

evidence.publisher: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
evidence.paraphrase: CODE reports a 12-week accelerator for more than ten early-stage startups offering integrated software solutions for Saudi sectors.

resources.name: Monsha'at Business Accelerators Program
resources.discovery_method: Use the service guide to identify accelerator channels, then inspect Monsha'at service-provider and virtual-lab pages for named product builders and prototype providers.
resources.expected_yield: Broad cross-sector entrepreneur and SME intake; more useful for source discovery than direct founder extraction.
resources.notes: A Monsha'at virtual-lab provider page independently confirms Sanadk as an AI accounting platform serving SMEs.

evidence.paraphrase: The guide defines three-to-six-month accelerator programs for entrepreneurs and SMEs and explains that applicants select an accelerator through Monsha'at.

resources.name: NTDP startup-support products
resources.discovery_method: Track Empowering Accelerators, MVP Lab, Bridge, AIM, and Saudi Unicorns for partner accelerators, beneficiary stories, portfolio interviews, and new cohort announcements.
resources.expected_yield: Cross-program map to startups receiving innovation, growth, finance, talent, and market-access support.
resources.notes: NTDP supports the Flat6Labs Riyadh Seed Program and hosts multiple products that can reveal startups at different maturity stages.

evidence.paraphrase: NTDP lists innovation, growth, financing, talent, and market-access products including MVP Lab, Empowering Accelerators, Bridge, and Saudi Unicorns.

resources.name: Sanabil Accelerator by 500 Global

resources.notes: Useful for later discovery, but MENA eligibility alone is not Saudi-market proof.

evidence.paraphrase: The Riyadh program targets MENA technology startups with an MVP and early traction and offers a 12-week growth program with potential investment.

gaps.detail: This lane produced 26 post-cutoff raw candidates plus four older or undated Misk alumni, for 30 total records. It did not pad the list with unnamed CODE or Garage cohort members.

Many accelerator finalists already operate mature software products or have visible technical teams. They are valuable raw candidates and source exemplars, but should not automatically become active outreach leads.
Sanadk has no confirmed founder in the reviewed public sources. Nero and Rintel have named people associated with the companies, but their decision authority was not confirmed.
TAQADAM is global. Bellboy, Atomica AI, TileGreen, InnoTech, and VitruvianMD need evidence of actual Saudi incorporation, customers, pilots, or operating teams before lead activation.
Unknown remains unknown. Absence of a visible CTO or engineering team was never treated as proof that technical capacity is absent.

The Garage, CODE, Monsha'at, and NTDP are high-value repeatable sources but their public pages did not expose complete named cohort directories in this pass; monitor their announcements and public social feeds at graduation points.
Observed-yield counts overlap where one candidate was discovered through a cohort page and verified through a partner program. They are source contribution counts, not additive unique totals.
